title: MCP vs REST and GraphQL for AI
description: Compare MCP with REST and GraphQL when building AI-ready backend interfaces.

blocks.text: REST and GraphQL are excellent for web and mobile clients. MCP is purpose-built for AI clients that need capability discovery, structured tool calling, and prompt composition. In practice, many systems expose all three.

cards.title: REST
cards.description: Resource-oriented HTTP endpoints with JSON payloads.

cards.title: GraphQL
cards.description: Schema-driven query language for flexible data retrieval.

cards.title: MCP
cards.description: Protocol for AI clients to discover and use backend capabilities.

blocks.title: Use each for its strength
blocks.text: Serve REST or GraphQL to web clients. Add MCP where AI clients, agents, or automation platforms need structured discovery and tool use.

items.text: I can name a scenario where REST is better than MCP
items.hint: Public web API consumed by mobile apps

items.text: I can name a scenario where MCP is better than REST
items.hint: AI agent that must discover available tools dynamically

items.text: I understand why systems often expose both
items.hint: Different clients have different needs; MCP complements rather than replaces REST

blocks.title: Lesson Summary
points: REST and GraphQL remain the best choice for general-purpose APIs.
MCP adds AI-specific capability discovery and tool calling.
The best backend often exposes both protocols.
blocks.takeaway: Do not replace existing APIs with MCP. Add MCP where AI clients need structured, discoverable interfaces.
